> Since the unload steps run on all descendants, event handlers like `pagehide` will fire on nested Documents as well. While `pageconceal` will only fire on the "displayed document". I have a few questions about that:
> 
> * Is the inconsistency with `pagehide` ok? If we expect authors to switch over to `pageconceal` to handle both VT and non-VT associated navigations.

It's consistent with *navigations*. Those unloading iframes are not navigating anywhere. `pageconceal` is designed to only be fired when you have a document on both sides. For other use-cases `pagehide` is still there :)

> * I'm not sure what "entry" corresponds to in the "activation" provided to nested Documents.

For the same reason, the nested document don't "activate" anything so they don't have an activation nor an event :)

> * What does "displayedDocument" correspond to? Is this the top-level Document in that window or the Document displayed in the frame (navigable?) being navigated. VT is supported for iframes so we need `pageconceal` to work on iframes as well.

It's the document being navigated away from, not necessarily the top-level document. It can certainly be an iframe.

I ran into an issue while implementing this. We don't create the NavigationHistoryEntry for a navigation on the old Document, so `entry` here is not initialized currently. It'll only happen if this Document is persisted into the BFCache and then reactivated while executing: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#update-the-navigation-api-entries-for-reactivation.

It also seems unnecessarily complicated to require a NavigationHistoryEntry for the new Document on the old Document. So the other option you mentioned is indeed better: "a destination + navigationType in the event", where destination is NavigationDestination (which is also in the `navigate` event). Except now it will have the final URL. NavigationDestination looks perfect because it provides the id to look up the NavigationHistoryEntry if its a traverse navigation.

We create it in this spec! https://whatpr.org/html/10002/6a9aef0...c6554ef/browsing-the-web.html#revealing-and-concealing-the-document:

`If  targetEntry  's  origin is same origin with  document  's origin, a new NavigationHistoryEntry in  document's relevant realm with its session history entry set to  targetEntry`

This is equivalent to how it's done on `navigation.activation` when the `from` entry is not in the list of entries.

Why is creating a `destination` less complicated than creating a `NavigationHistoryEntry`.

We can discuss using a `NavigationDestination` instead of a `NavigationHistoryEntry` in terms of ergonomics, but there should not be a big difference in terms of complexity.

Actually wait, there's another fundamental limitation that needs to be captured here: the new Document cannot be activated until the callback passed to "setting up a cross-document view-transition" is invoked. For non-prerendering case, that also implies that the new Document shouldn't execute script.

When "setting up a cross-document view-transition" is called, the algorithm will wait until the next rendering opportunity to cache the Document's visual state and then dispatch the callback. The old Document must be the "active" navigation entry until this point where active implies this is the Document displayed to the user. The last frame we cache must be the last visual state shown to the user. Since there can be only 1 active Document for a navigable, the new Document can't become active until then.

For non-prerender, when the new Document starts executing script it also assumes its active. This matters because certain APIs require the Document to be active. So if we start executing script on the new Document but not make it active, APIs might not behave as expected. Pre-rendering also has this problem except there the author is aware that the Document is in "pre-rendered" state and can structure their logic accordingly.

It's possible the spec text here already takes care of this (hard for me to follow) but I wanted to be explicit about the intent.

If we do decide to hide both `entry` and `navigationType` in the cross-origin case based on https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9702#issuecomment-1923489553 then maybe its cleaner to not change NavigationActivation and instead make `activation` here nullable? `from` is already trivially accessible as the current NavigationHistoryEntry so the struct is really for the destination entry and nav type.
